previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a male with HCV cirrhosis, was admitted for increasing abdominal distension and hematuria. Imaging confirmed large ascites and cholelithiasis without cholecystitis. A paracentesis removed 2.5 liters of fluid, which showed no signs of infection, ruling out spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. His hematuria resolved during admission and was attributed to low platelets from cirrhosis and HCV therapy. Due to persistent thrombocytopenia, his ribavirin, interferon, and filgrastim were discontinued. Diuretic therapy was intensified with furosemide and spironolactone, and he was advised on a strict low-salt diet. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans to follow up with hepatology and urology.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with HCV cirrhosis complicated by portal HTN and esophageal 
varices s/p recent banding who presented with hematochezia with 
subsequent hematemesis from upper GI bleed.

Active Issues:

#. Upper GI bleed:  He was admitted to the MICU due to concern 
for variceal bleed.  His Hct dropped from 34.0 to 29.3 and he 
was transfused 2 units PRBCS with appropriate response.  He was 
started on an octreotide drip, ceftriaxone, and IV PPI drip.  He 
underwent EGD in the MICU which showed blood in the stomach, 
known esophageal varices that were not bleeding, and an 
esophageal ulcer without active bleeding.  His previous banding 
of the varices were no longer in place.  His hematocrit 
subsequently remained stable and his diet was advanced the next 
day.  His ceftriaxone was changed to ciprofloxacin with plans 
for ___lso started on sucralfate for 5 days after 
the procedure.  His IV pantoprazole drip was changed to IV PPI 
BID and then to 40mg po bid to be continued after discharge.  He 
has an appointment in 2 weeks for follow-up EGD with Dr. ___.  
Nadolol was held during the admission due to bradycardia, but 
restarted at discharge.

#. HCV Cirrhosis: He has known hepatitis C cirrhosis without 
evidence of decompensation.  His diuretics and nadolol were held 
given his GI bleed and bradycardia.  He was continued on his ___ 
___.

#. Bradycardia: He had bradycardia while in the MICU that was 
sinus on ECG.  It was felt to be liekly related to his 
octreotide infusion.  His nadolol was held due to his 
bradycardia, but his HR improved upon discontinuation of the 
octreotide and nadolol was restarted on discharge.  He was 
monitored on telemetry throughout admission.

Inactive Issues:

#. CAD s/p CABG: He remained asymptomatic and chest pain free.

#. DM: He was managed with humalog sliding scale while in house
